description: A BGP neighbour of the router, or the neighbours on a set of interfaces or of a prefix: where to reach them, their AS, and what the router accepts from them and sends them in each address family.

address.description: Unicast address of the neighbour beyond the router, neither loopback, link-local nor IPv4-mapped; excludes `interface`, `interfaces` and `listen`.

x-chalkos-rules.description: A BGPPeer's address is a unicast address beyond the router: not unspecified, loopback, link-local, multicast, broadcast or IPv4-mapped IPv6.
x-chalkos-rules.messageExpression: "the address " + self + " is no neighbour's: give a unicast address beyond the router, neither loopback, link-local nor IPv4-mapped; a neighbour on a link takes interface or interfaces"

bfd.description: Whether the router checks the session's link with BFD, at the timers of the BGP document, and ends the session when BFD finds it down.

description.description: What the neighbour is, in up to 80 printable ASCII characters other than `@`, with a single space between two words.

x-chalkos-rules.description: A BGPPeer's description holds 80 characters at most.
x-chalkos-rules.message: the description holds more than 80 characters

extendedNextHop.description: Whether the router sends and accepts IPv4 routes with IPv6 next hops (RFC 8950). A peer at an IPv6 address or with an IPv6 listen range that exchanges IPv4 routes needs it. FRR negotiates it on sessions of `interface` and `interfaces` whatever this says.

families.description: The address families the session exchanges routes of, and how.

defaultOriginate.description: Whether the router sends the peer a default route of the family: whatever its own table holds, or while `defaultOriginateWhen` holds.

defaultOriginateWhen.description: PrefixList of the family that decides when the router sends the default route of `defaultOriginate`: while the peer's VRF holds a route the list matches, from BGP, from the kernel, such as a route from DHCP, from router advertisements or a `Network`'s `[Route]`, or a link's prefix. Blackhole, unreachable and prohibit routes do not count. The router does not announce the routes it tracks. null sends the default route whatever the table holds.

export.description: RoutingPolicy that decides the routes the router sends the peer; null sends every route the router has.

import.description: RoutingPolicy that decides the routes the router accepts from the peer; null accepts every route.

maxPrefix.description: Routes the router accepts from the peer at most; past them it ends the session. null sets no limit.

ipv4.description: IPv4 routes of the session; null exchanges none.

ipv6.description: IPv6 routes of the session; null exchanges none.

interface.description: Interface on whose link the router finds the neighbour by its IPv6 link-local address, without an address of its own on the link; excludes `address`, `interfaces` and `listen`. A name that reads as an address is refused.

x-chalkos-rules.description: A BGPPeer's interfaces are not named like addresses.

interfaces.description: Interfaces, by name or glob, a glob being a prefix followed by `*`, with a session each, as for `interface`; a glob stands for the interfaces of the peer's VRF that the node's Network documents name in a `[Match]` section's `Name=`. range.description: Prefix whose addresses may open a session with the router; neither link-local, loopback, multicast nor IPv4-mapped.

listen.description: Accept a session from every neighbour whose address lies in `range`, which then shares the peer's settings; the router opens no session itself. Excludes `address`, `interface` and `interfaces`.

password.description: Key of a Secret that holds the session's TCP MD5 password, of 80 characters at most and no white space; null for none. The Secret's name and key hold letters, digits, `.`, `_` and `-` alone.

remoteAS.description: AS of the neighbour: a number, `external` for any AS but the router's, or `internal` for the router's own.

shutdown.description: Whether the router keeps the session down while the document stays.

vrf.description: VRF document whose BGP instance runs the session; `default` for the default VRF. The peer's interfaces are links of that VRF.
